title: Absolute marked tests versus Joyal categorical equivalences
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, functor quasicategories and cores of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and markings and absolute marked weak equivalences of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. For every map $b:B	o E$ from a small simplicial set to a small quasicategory, its canonical marked map $B^ lat	o E^
atural$ is an absolute marked weak equivalence if and only if $b$ is a categorical equivalence. Here $ lat$ marks only degenerate edges and $
atural$ marks the equivalence edges. More generally a simplicial map $c:C	o E$ between quasicategories is a categorical equivalence if and only if its marked map $C^
atural	o E^
atural$ is an absolute marked weak equivalence.

For an arbitrary map $t:A	o B$ of small simplicial sets, $t$ is a categorical equivalence if and only if for every quasicategory $Q$ in any sufficiently large universe the precomposition map $\operatorname{Fun}(B,Q)^\simeq	o\operatorname{Fun}(A,Q)^\simeq$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. All assertions remain true after enlargement of the universe and include empty simplicial sets.

source.place: HTT Proposition 3.1.3.5 over a point and Proposition 3.2.2.14; core testing formulation used for the vertex fibers. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result; HTT is requested in report.md.

proof.text:
First fix a universe containing the input simplicial sets. For every simplicial set $K$ and quasicategory $Q$, there is a natural identity $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(K^ lat,Q^
atural)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)^\simeq$. Indeed $\operatorname{Map}^{ lat}(K^ lat,Q^
atural)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ degree by degree: the only marked edges in $K^ lat	imes(\Delta^n)^ lat$ are degenerate, so preservation of markings imposes no condition on a simplicial map. The marked-anodyne lifting calculus identifies its $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}$ with its core. For a quasicategory $C$, the point-model statement separately gives $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(C^
atural,Q^
atural)=\operatorname{Fun}(C,Q)^\simeq$. Both identifications commute with restriction, since they leave the underlying simplicial maps unchanged.

source.place: Remark 3.1.3.1 over a point; direct degreewise calculation of the minimal marking.

proof.text: Let $t:A\to B$ be categorical and fix a quasicategory $Q$. By the functor-equivalence test, $p=t^*:\operatorname{Fun}(B,Q)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,Q)$ admits a coherent quasi-inverse $s$, with equivalence edges between the two composites and the identities. Simplicial maps preserve equivalences because they preserve the inverse edges and their two witness triangles, so $p,s$ restrict to cores. The unit and counit restrict to simplicial homotopies on these cores: evaluation of either transformation on an equivalence edge of the source gives a square whose horizontal components and vertical source images are equivalences. Its two triangular faces express the diagonal as a composite of equivalences; the triangle calculus therefore makes every image edge an equivalence. Thus the evaluation maps on the core times $\Delta^1$ land in the core. The simplicial-homotopy-equivalence lemma now shows that $p^\simeq$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The functor-cone calculus guarantees that all functor objects and cores used here are quasicategories and Kan complexes, respectively.

source.place: Proposition 1.2.7.3(3); the forward implication of Lemma 3.1.3.2, with restriction to cores written out.

proof.text: Conversely suppose all the core tests for $t$ are weak homotopy equivalences. Fix $Q$ and put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(B,Q)$, $E=\operatorname{Fun}(A,Q)$, $p=t^*:D\to E$. These are quasicategories by the functor-equivalence test. For every small simplicial set $K$, apply the hypothesis to the quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$. Currying and interchanging the $K$ and $A$ or $B$ factors identifies the tested map with $\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)^\simeq$, induced by postcomposition with $p$. In particular this map is bijective on components. Components of a simplicial set are vertices modulo finite edge paths, as follows directly from its realization by connected simplices. In these Kan cores a finite edge path can be replaced by a single edge in either orientation: reverse an edge by filling a two-dimensional outer horn with a degenerate side, and concatenate two edges by filling an inner two-horn. Edges of these cores are exactly coherent natural equivalences. Thus the component bijections just obtained are bijections on functors modulo coherent natural equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3.2 and the exponential argument in Proposition 3.1.3.3; explicit currying for arbitrary domains.

proof.text: Take $K=E$ in the preceding component bijection. Surjectivity lifts the component of $1_E$ to a functor $s:E\to D$ with $ps\simeq1_E$. For $K=D$, the functors $sp$ and $1_D$ have images $psp$ and $p$ in the same component, by whiskering this natural equivalence with $p$. Injectivity of that component map gives $sp\simeq1_D$. Therefore $s$ is a coherent quasi-inverse for the specified $p$. The equivalences are actual equivalence edges after the Kan horn concatenations of step 3. This construction applies for each $Q$, so condition (ii) of the functor-equivalence test implies that $t$ is categorical. Together with step 2 this proves the arbitrary-simplicial-set core-testing assertion.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3.2: the two test objects and inverse construction, applied after currying.

proof.text: Now let $b:B\to E$ with $E$ a quasicategory. For every test quasicategory $Q$, step 1 identifies restriction along $B^\flat\to E^\natural$ with the specified map $\operatorname{Fun}(E,Q)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,Q)^\simeq$. By the point-model definition, the marked map is a weak equivalence exactly when all these restriction maps are weak homotopy equivalences. Steps 2--4 identify precisely that condition with $b$ being categorical. The marked map exists since it only has to preserve degenerate edges.

source.place: Definition 3.1.3.4 over a point, combined with Remark 3.1.3.1 and the core test proved above.

proof.text: For $c:C\to E$ between quasicategories, preservation of the inverse-triangle witnesses ensures that $c$ preserves equivalence edges and hence defines $C^\natural\to E^\natural$. The natural-natural identity in step 1 identifies each marked restriction test with $\operatorname{Fun}(E,Q)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(C,Q)^\simeq$. The point-model weak-equivalence test and steps 2--4 again give exactly the stated equivalence with $c$ categorical. No fibrant replacement of $C$ or $E$ is needed.

source.place: Definition 3.1.3.4 and Proposition 3.1.3.5 over a point; use the literal mapping-core identity.

proof.text: All constructions above can be made in each containing universe. In steps 3--4 the new tests $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$, $D$ and $E$ are in that universe, since its small sets are closed under products, function sets and countable degree indexing. The functor-equivalence test quantifies over the same sufficiently large universes, and the point-model statement explicitly preserves its weak-equivalence tests under enlargement. Thus the proved equivalences persist under enlargement. No step selects a vertex of an input simplicial set: step 4 selects the identity functors, which exist even on the empty quasicategory. For $\varnothing\to\varnothing$ every tested core is a point; for $\varnothing\to B$ with $B$ nonempty, the test $Q=\varnothing$ is $\varnothing\to\Delta^0$ and fails. This verifies that no implicit nonemptiness hypothesis has entered.

source.place: Universe-relative application of the displayed tests; empty-domain and empty-target checks.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q157-35efb6aa3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full and wrote review.md; I made no changes. The statement is unchanged and true: absolute marked tests B^flat->E^natural and C^natural->E^natural, and the core test Fun(B,Q)^≃->Fun(A,Q)^≃ for categorical equivalence. Small cases agree on both sides: empty->empty, empty->nonempty fails at Q=empty, and Delta^1->Delta^0 is correctly separated. Step 1: the minimal product marking forces Map^flat(K^flat,Q^natural)=Fun(K,Q); the anodyne calculus says Map^sharp is its core, and the point model gives Map^sharp(C^natural,D^natural)=Fun(C,D)^≃. Step 2: the functor test (ii) supplies a quasi-inverse. I checked edge by edge that the unit and counit restrict to the cores, using the pointwise criterion of the cone calculus and the triangle calculus for diagonal edges; the simplicial-homotopy lemma then gives the weak equivalence. Steps 3-4: currying turns the test into postcomposition with p on Fun(K,D)^≃ and Fun(K,E)^≃, Kan cores turn component bijections into classes up to coherent natural equivalence, and K=E then K=D build s with ps≃1 and sp≃1 for the specified p, which is condition (ii). Steps 5-6 are elementary from the point-model definition. Step 7 bridges small C and larger universes through the point model's enlargement clause. A DFS over the dependencies (472 nodes) finds no cycle. An rg search of the DAG finds no duplicate; I read four candidates and none states this test. No new nodes and no SGA sources. lean.statement: theorem marked_flat_categorical_equivalence_test : (∀ {B E : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory E] (b : B ⟶ E), weak (flatMap b ≫ flatToMarked (natural E)) ↔ ∀ (Q : SSet.{max u v}), Q.Quasicategory → ((hoFunctor.map ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map b)).app Q)).toFunctor).IsEquivalence) ∧ (∀ {C E : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory C] [Quasicategory E] (c : C ⟶ E), weak (naturalMap c) ↔ ∀ (Q : SSet.{max u v}), Q.Quasicategory → ((hoFunctor.map ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map c)).app Q)).toFunctor).IsEquivalence) ∧ (∀ {A B : SSet.{u}} (t : A ⟶ B), (∀ (Q : SSet.{max u v}), Q.Quasicategory → ((hoFunctor.map ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map t)).app Q)).toFunctor).IsEquivalence) ↔ ∀ (Q : SSet.{max u v}), Q.Quasicategory → Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (Enhanced.coreMap ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map t)).app Q)))
lean.note: Uses the exact Joyal homotopy-category testing formula from the recorded Joyal model statement. naturalMap constructs the canonical natural-marking map on the given underlying simplicial map; all data are explicit.
